Title: Sunline Kantan Cast Braid X8
Description:
Sunline Kantan Cast Braid X8

Diameter chart, reel capacity & backing guide

Kantan Cast Braid X8 is Sunline's braid for repeated casting and power-fishing presentations such as pitching, flipping and frogs. This guide covers the verified 30 and 50 lb US rows, each in 150- and 600-yard packages.

Construction
Eight-strand dark-green PE braid
Listed strengths
30-50 lb
Line type
Braid main line

Does Kantan fit your casting setup?

Start with the rod, lure and cover, then compare how much working line the reel can hold. The 50 lb option needs more spool space per yard than 30 lb. A larger label is not a substitute for matching the entire setup.

Choosing your setup

Choosing your Kantan Cast Braid X8 strength

30 lb is listed at .296 mm; 50 lb is .382 mm. Select the actual row before estimating the fill, especially with a shallow spool.

The 30 lb spool pictured identifies the family. It does not mean the 50 lb row has the same diameter or that every strength shares one label.

A short leader does not change the diameter of the braid occupying most of the spool. Calculate with the main line, then choose the leader for the presentation.

Specification-based setup guidance, not a hands-on casting, abrasion or breaking-strength test.

Backing, working line & leaders

Choose the working section first

Allow for the longest cast, fish runs and later trimming. Compare that total with the chosen package; a 150-yard supply need not fill the reel to its full braid capacity.

Use backing deliberately

Follow the reel maker's arbor-attachment guidance. When using mono backing, leave space for the intended braid section rather than winding an arbitrary amount underneath it.

Treat bulk length as a budget

A 600-yard spool can be divided among planned fills. Four 150-yard portions are not necessarily four suitable reel fills; account for each reel and attachment allowance.

Kantan Cast Braid X8 questions, answered

Is Kantan Cast Braid X8 fluorocarbon?

No. It is braid. Sunline's handling comparison does not change its material identity.

Why are only 30 and 50 lb shown?

These are the coherent source-verified rows used here. The 40 and 60 lb manufacturer inch/mm entries still need clarification. No 65 lb variant was established in the checked US listing.

Does the photograph show every package?

No. It shows the original 30 lb, 150-yard spool. The manufacturer separately lists both included strengths in 150- and 600-yard packages.

Specifications & sources

The Sunline America product chart and assigned variants provide the numeric evidence. The dealer-hosted original spool label supplies exact-family imagery. No retailer-authored diameter correction is used.

Calculations use the catalog's listed inch diameters. Published inch and millimeter values may differ slightly because of rounding.

30 lb

Plan around the 30 lb package you have

Use this reference when your package matches SDB30G-150 and its printed size. A 150-yard spool can supply the whole braid section or leave a remainder, depending on reel capacity, backing and the reserve you need. The nominal strength is one part of the choice; check it against your rod, reel and intended fishing before filling.

Backing, working line & leaders

Match the original package

Check SDB30G-150, 30 lb and .28 mm together. The photographed spool also carries SAP 1556099 and UPC 022021647286.

Choose your working length

Allow for your longest cast, a fish taking line, trimming and retying. A 150-yard package does not require a 150-yard fill.

Secure the spool connection

Follow the reel maker's braid attachment instructions. Where needed, start with monofilament backing and place the connection below the braid used during a cast.

Check the finished fill

Wind evenly under appropriate tension and stop at the reel maker's specified clearance. Inspect the line and knots before use; a legible label does not establish the condition of stored line.

DuraBraid questions, answered

Does 10 lb Test Dia mean this is 10 lb braid?

No. The package identifies the braid as 30 lb. Its 10 lb Test Dia phrase compares its size with monofilament; .011 in / .28 mm is the separate physical diameter.

Can I use these diameters for a different DuraBraid spool?

Only if that spool has its own matching manufacturer label or specification. This guide is limited to SDB30G-150, 30 lb Moss Green and 150 yards.

Are these current-stock specifications?

The original photo is undated. Its identifiers also appear in the manufacturer US feed, but that does not establish the age, condition or uninterrupted formulation of a particular spool.

Will the entire 150-yard package fit?

That depends on usable reel capacity and any backing. Plan the braid section first, check the estimate and leave the reel maker's specified clearance.

Backing, working line & leaders

Read both numbers on the label

Match the nominal pound test and physical mm diameter on the blue EZ Braid package. The smaller Test Dia pound figure is a comparison with monofilament.

Budget the working section

Start with cast distance plus reserve for a run, trimming and retying. Keep that total within the 110-yard package and the reel's usable capacity.

Add backing where needed

Follow the reel maker's braid attachment instructions. Calculate backing below the chosen braid section, and keep the connection below the line used during casting.

Check before fishing

Wind evenly under appropriate tension and stop at the specified spool clearance. Inspect stored line and test your knots before use.

EZ Braid questions, answered

Which label number is the braid strength?

Use the large 10, 15, 20 or 30 lb rating. The smaller 3, 4, 6 or 8 lb Test Dia figure compares diameter with monofilament; it does not rename the braid.

Is the inch diameter printed on the package?

The reviewed EZ Braid labels print millimeters. The inch values in this guide are calculated from those millimeter values, not separately published measurements.

Can I use the European kg chart instead?

Not as a direct replacement. That historical range has its own SAPs, diameters, lengths and kg strength column, without a nominal-US-pound mapping.

Does this cover 300-yard or yellow packages?

No. The numeric source photos show only 110-yard Moss Green packages. Other packages need matching original evidence.

Are these current-production specifications?

The photographs are undated and their front labels do not expose individual SKUs. This reference does not establish manufacture date, storage condition or continuity with every later package.

Can I use the fluorocarbon Contra chart?

Backing, working line & leaders

Budget the 150 yards

Leave enough working braid for your longest cast, expected run and future trimming. For a 100-yard working section, a new 150-yard spool leaves 50 yards before knots and trimming; it is not a second equal fill.

Choose backing from the actual diameter

SuperPower Braid questions, answered

Is this the Texas Edition line?

Does a 300-yard option contain 327 yards?

The separate original 30 lb listing has a 300-yard option but a 327-yard title and item-length field. The artwork also advertises extra yardage. That conflicting package is excluded; this guide accepts only separately checked 150-yard children.

Why are some strengths missing?

The 12/25 lb chart values reverse adjacent strength diameters. The 65/80 lb titles conflict with the strand-count image. Those sizes need exact corroborating labels before they can join this guide.

No equivalence is established here. The recovered manufacturer artwork says DESTRON MONOFILAMENT and specifies quarter-pound spools. The Essential product has its own name and 300-yard variants.

The inspected manufacturer chart prints 1,628 yards, .011 inch and .28 mm. The retrieved US listing title also says 15 lb/1,628 yards. A secondary search mirror carrying 1,050 yards is not used as evidence for this package.

Does this mean original Destron is available now?

No. The checked Amazon listing says currently unavailable. The recovered chart and package establish an original product specification scope, not present retail stock or an official discontinuation date.
